title: Pipelines as DAGs: Operating Airflow
intro: A training pipeline is a chain of steps: extract data, validate it, build features, train, evaluate, register. Orchestrators such as Airflow, Kubeflow Pipelines, and Argo Workflows describe that chain as a DAG (a graph of tasks with dependencies), then schedule, retry, and record it. Airflow is the most widely used. The DAG here is retrain_churn_model.

steps.prompt: List the DAGs Airflow has loaded.
steps.fake_output:
dag_id               | filepath              | owner   | paused
=====================+=======================+=========+=======
retrain_churn_model  | retrain_churn.py      | ml-team | False
nightly_features     | nightly_features.py   | ml-team | False
steps.why: A DAG file is Python that Airflow parses on a loop. A new DAG that doesn't appear here was either not picked up or failed to parse, which the next step checks.

steps.prompt: A colleague's new DAG isn't in the list. Check for DAG files that failed to import.
steps.fake_output:
filepath                 | error
=========================+==================================================================
/dags/score_customers.py | ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'feast'
steps.explanation: score_customers.py imports a package that isn't installed on the scheduler.
steps.why: Import errors are silent in the DAG list: the DAG simply isn't there. Because the scheduler re-parses DAG files constantly, heavy work at the top of a DAG file (database calls, loading a model) also slows every other DAG. Keep the top level cheap.

steps.prompt: Run one task on its own, without recording the run or its dependencies: the train task of retrain_churn_model for the logical date 2026-09-27.
steps.fake_output:
[2026-09-28 10:02:11] INFO - loading features for 2026-09-27
[2026-09-28 10:04:40] INFO - trained model auc=0.871
[2026-09-28 10:04:41] INFO - Marking task as SUCCESS
steps.explanation: The task ran for that date and passed, with nothing written to Airflow's database.
steps.why: 'tasks test' is the debugging tool: one task, in the foreground, with logs on your terminal. The date matters: every run has a logical date, the period of data it covers, and a task should use it rather than 'now'. That's what makes a run repeatable.

steps.prompt: The feature data for 20 to 26 September was corrected upstream. Re-run the DAG for those dates.
steps.fake_output: [backfill progress] | finished run 7 of 7 | tasks waiting: 0 | succeeded: 42 | failed: 0
steps.explanation: Seven daily runs were re-executed, each for its own date.
steps.why: Backfill only works if tasks are idempotent: running the 23rd again must overwrite the 23rd's output, not append to it. Write to a location or partition named by the logical date. Tasks that use 'today' or append blindly are the main reason pipelines can't be safely re-run.

steps.prompt: Trigger a run now, outside the schedule.
steps.why: A pipeline also needs a gate before a new model replaces the old one: compare the evaluation metric with the current production model and stop if it's worse (mlops-tutorial-010 covers the rollout). 'The pipeline succeeded' only means the code ran, not that the model is better.
